segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
86. to the war with the Arabs:
And he entered Constantinople,
and was confirmed in the kingdom.
Then John Tzimiskes the Domesticus came against Mopsuestia,
and encamped against it for seven days.
And he made in its wall more than sixty breaches,
yet he was not able to enter it;
but he burned its district and the district of Adana and of Tarsus.
And five thousand men who were coming from Tarsus to the help of the people of Mopsuestia,
the Romans fell upon them and killed them all,
and they left and went away.
And there was a great famine in Cilicia,
and a multitude of the Arab people left and fled to Damascus.
And also in Aleppo and in Harran and in Edessa there was a severe famine.
And after a year, the Domesticus came again to Cilicia,
and sat against Mopsuestia for three months,
and was not able to conquer it.
Rather, he imposed {OCR?} a tribute upon it, and they went away,
on account of the sickness and the pestilence that had broken out among his armies.
And in the year one thousand two hundred and seventy-six,
1276 of the Greeks,
(965 of our Lord?),
which is the year three hundred and fifty-four,
354 of the Arabs,
Nicephorus the king went forth from Constantinople,
and came and resided in Caesarea of Cappadocia.
And the people of Tarsus and Mopsuestia sent to him that they would submit to him,
and that he should send from him someone who should rule over them.
He, however, replied:
"Now that you have cut off hope of help from your Arab kings,
and have eaten dead dogs from famine,
and the pestilence has brought you to an end,
do you submit to me?
Until you grow strong and rebel? You have nothing from me except the sword!"
And when he had burned their letter on the head of their envoy,
and his beard also was burned,
he drove him away.
It is said
that three hundred biers of the dead were going out every day from Tarsus.
Then King Nicephorus gathered his armies {OCR?},
and entered and encamped against Mopsuestia,
and conquered it on Saturday the 13th
of Rajab, the month of this year of the Arabs.
And he made a great slaughter in it,
and took captive two hundred thousand human beings, men, women, and children,
and sent them to the country of the Romans.
And he came and encamped against Tarsus.
